status: review studies; not gameplay definitions or historical eligibility. size is the pixel budget for the family at the character's scale (~17px per metre).

families.name: Plain earthen pot
families.description: A squat rounded pot with a thick uneven rim, dark opening and a few clustered firing marks.

families.name: Large storage jar
families.description: A broad-bellied jar with a narrow shoulder and removable clay or fiber lid.

families.name: Handled water jug
families.description: A narrow-necked jug with one readable loop handle and a bright highlight along its shoulder.

families.name: Transport amphora
families.description: An elongated vessel with two strong handles, a small sealed mouth and a visibly supported base.

families.name: Glazed jar
families.description: A rounded storage vessel with a darker foot, glossy clustered highlights and an optional simple painted band.

families.name: Metal water vessel
families.description: A rounded metal vessel with a turned collar, deep opening and sharply contrasting reflected bands.

families.name: Storage vat
families.description: A vat sunk to its shoulder in the floor, over a metre across the rim: a household's whole year of grain or oil.

families.name: Stoppered flask
families.description: A small flask with a cork and a carrying cord: what a traveller takes, not what a house keeps.

families.name: Open bowl
families.description: A wide shallow bowl, most of what you see being the inside of it.

families.name: Cooking pot
families.description: A three-legged pot with a bail handle: soot on the shaded side, the fire-lit belly catching light down its left.

families.name: Gourd vessel
families.description: An asymmetric natural gourd with a cut opening, mottled surface and optional fiber carrying loop.

families.name: Open work basket
families.description: A shallow oval basket with a thick woven rim and large, legible bands of wicker.

families.name: Lidded storage basket
families.description: A taller woven container with a distinct fitted lid, binding straps and a shaded lower edge.

families.name: Sack or hide bag
families.description: A slumped soft container with gathered folds, a tied neck and material-specific cloth or hide shading.

families.name: Plain wooden box
families.description: A low rectangular box with a lift-off lid, broad boards and simple corner joints.

families.name: Large bound chest
families.description: A heavier chest with a hinged lid, two dark reinforcing bands and a clearly visible fastening.

families.name: Strapped chest
families.description: A smaller trunk seen square on: domed lid in board courses, two iron straps riveted lid to plinth, brass lock plate.

families.name: Painted wooden chest
families.description: A raised or footed chest with colored panels and restrained trim that changes its silhouette from the plain box.

families.name: Barrel
families.description: A bulging stave-built barrel with an elliptical top, dark hoops and a small bung or lid.

families.name: Transport crate
families.description: An open-slatted rectangular crate with thick corner posts and visible gaps between boards.

families.name: Bucket or pail
families.description: A stave-built wooden pail with a curved metal handle, wooden grip, open mouth and iron hoops.

families.name: Water or feed trough
families.description: A long low receptacle with a deep shaded interior and separately authored hollowed-wood or masonry forms.

families.name: Low well or cistern mouth
families.description: A low masonry shaft with staggered stone courses, chipped capstones and a recessed opening.

families.name: Timber-framed well
families.description: A water opening beneath two posts and a crossbeam, with a clear rope-and-bucket silhouette and optional small roof.

families.name: Public town well
families.description: A broad public wellhead with a swing arm, a bucket on the rope and grass breaking through the kerb; the size a town square carries.

families.name: Hand pump
families.description: A compact upright pump with a curved handle, projecting spout and a small stained base.

families.name: Grinding stone and handstone
families.description: A low stone slab with a worn hollow and a smaller contrasting handstone resting across it.

families.name: Mortar and pestle
families.description: A deep stone or wooden bowl with a thick rim and a pestle angled against its edge.

families.name: Hoe or digging tool
families.description: A long worn handle ends in a clearly shaped working head, with separate stone, composite and metal forms.

families.name: Pickaxe
families.description: A hafted head that crosses the handle: one arm a point for rock, the other a narrow chisel.

families.name: Sickle
families.description: A short gripped handle supports a strongly curved cutting edge, with distinct composite and metal constructions.

families.name: Shovel or spade
families.description: A straight handle ends in a broad readable blade, differentiated through wooden and metal head shapes.

families.name: Rake
families.description: A head of teeth on a shaft as long as a man, stood where it was last left.

families.name: Pitchfork
families.description: Tines on an iron socket for hay or muck.

families.name: Spear
families.description: A hunting spear stood on its butt, the blade a leaf of stone or metal.

families.name: Long shovel
families.description: A navvy's shovel: a long haft and a broad dished blade that opens two spits at a stroke.

families.name: Scythe
families.description: An S-curved snath with two nibs and a long blade that lays a swathe.

families.name: Firewood pile
families.description: A compact stack of irregular logs shows bright cut ends, dark bark and gaps between pieces.

families.name: Harvest bundle
families.description: A tied sheaf of crop-specific stalks fans out above and below a narrow binding.

families.name: Day's catch
families.description: Two fish on a hand-line, carried from the water to the drying rack and taken down again when they are dry.

families.name: Drying rack
families.description: A lightweight pole frame carries a few separated hanging objects or a shallow woven drying surface.

families.name: Bird-scaring figure or rig
families.description: A rough pole structure carries ragged cloth, fiber bundles or hanging strips appropriate to the selected tradition.

families.name: Open firepit
families.description: A ring of stones round an ash bed, two logs and a layered flame.

families.name: Communal bake oven
families.description: A clay dome on a stone base, its mouth glowing and a lick of flame at the lip.

families.name: Long fire
families.description: A trench of embers with three low flames along a single log, the fire of a cold-country camp.

families.name: Sunken clay oven
families.description: A clay cylinder set in a packed-earth collar, flame rising from its open top.

families.name: Standing brazier
families.description: A metal bowl on three splayed legs holding coals and a flame.

families.name: Brick stove and kettle
families.description: A brick block with a firebox in front and an iron kettle steaming on top.

families.name: Iron fire basket
families.description: A barred iron cage on legs with coals and a flame between the bars.

families.name: Oil-drum fire
families.description: A steel drum with rust and burn holes, flame standing out of its open top.

families.name: Oil lamp
families.description: A small vessel has a distinct wick nozzle, warm flame and a darkened patch around the burning edge.

families.name: Lantern
families.description: A framed lamp has a strong carrying loop and a warm central light behind locally appropriate panel construction.

families.name: Low stool
families.description: A compact seat rests on visibly separated legs, with wood, woven-seat or later metal variants.

families.name: Bench
families.description: A long simple seat has stout supports, a worn upper edge and optional locally selected backrest.

families.name: Table or workbench
families.description: A sturdy rectangular surface has clear legs, an overhanging edge and a few task-specific surface marks.

families.name: Anvil and block
families.description: A smith's anvil on a bound block: horn drawn out to the left, face struck smooth, iron hoop round the staves.

families.name: Upright loom
families.description: A standing loom nearly two metres tall: warp hanging taut from the top beam, woven cloth growing over the cloth beam, beater pressed down.

families.name: Sleeping mat or bedroll
families.description: A woven mat or rolled bedding has a soft folded edge, restrained stripes and a small raised pillow or bundle.

families.name: Metal canister or tin
families.description: A cylindrical or rectangular industrial container has folded seams, a distinct lid and restrained dents or rust.

families.name: Galvanised bin
families.description: A ribbed steel bin with a domed lid and a handle each side: the yard's refuse, from the factory age on.

families.name: Steel drum
families.description: A two-hundred-litre drum with rolling hoops and a bung: fuel, water or whatever else, rusting where it stands.

families.name: Wheelbarrow
families.description: A single-wheeled barrow with a flared tray and a handle bar: a yard, a building site, a smallholding.

families.name: Washing line
families.description: A line strung between two poles, pegged with washing that lifts in the wind.

families.name: Plastic bucket or bin
families.description: A molded container has a thick lip, simple handle or lid, and broad clean color blocks with modest scuffing.

families.name: Cardboard carton
families.description: A folded box has readable top flaps, dark crease lines and an optional plain packing mark or tape strip.

families.name: Torch post
families.description: A brand burning in an iron cresset on a timber post: what a gate or a market corner had before street lighting.

families.name: Brazier column
families.description: An iron fire basket on a stone column, lit at dusk by whoever the square pays to do it.

families.name: Lantern post
families.description: A paper lantern in a small roofed box on a timber post.

families.name: Gas lamp
families.description: A fluted cast-iron column with a ladder bar and four panes of glass: the eighteenth and nineteenth century street.

families.name: Electric street lamp
families.description: A swan neck and an enamel shade over a filament lamp, 1890 to the war.

families.name: Sodium lamp
families.description: A tapered steel column with a long arm and a cut-off head, the road since about 1960.

families.name: Trestle stall
families.description: Boards on trestles heaped with produce: the oldest and plainest way to sell anything.

families.name: Awning stall
families.description: A counter under a striped cloth on poles, with a valance over the front.

families.name: Market booth
families.description: A roofed kiosk with a boarded front and goods hung from the lintel.

families.name: Market cart
families.description: A two-wheeled cart tipped down to sell from, under a canvas tilt.

families.name: Market barrow
families.description: A tubular frame under a canvas tilt, crates below and a scale on the end.

families.name: Plough
families.description: A beam, a share and two handles: a scratch ard, a wheeled plough, or a steel mouldboard.

families.name: Water butt
families.description: A barrel under a downpipe with a tap at its foot.

families.name: Beehive
families.description: A coiled straw skep, or a box hive stacked on its stand.

families.name: Milk churn
families.description: A conical churn with a clamped lid and carrying handles.

families.name: Farm cart
families.description: A two-wheeled cart with its shafts down, standing in the yard.

families.name: Privy shed
families.description: A board shed over a pit, leaning a little, with a cut in the door and the spoil heaped behind it.

families.name: Screened pit
families.description: A reed or matting screen in a horseshoe round a pit, on poles.

families.name: Midden
families.description: No privy at all: the heap at the bottom of the yard, ash and sherds and bone, with a plank laid across it.

families.name: Dung heap
families.description: The farmyard muck heap, boarded in and forked over, with the straw still showing through.

families.name: Bench latrine
families.description: A stone bench of keyhole seats over a running channel: a town's public one.

families.name: Stone privy
families.description: A masonry privy block with a tiled roof and a chute down its side: the town house's own.

families.name: Night-soil privy
families.description: A shed with a collection hatch at the back, a tub and a carrying yoke: what comes out goes on the fields.

families.name: Brick outhouse
families.description: Brick, a slate roof, a cistern and a soil pipe.

families.name: Staddle granary
families.description: A boarded granary lifted clear of the ground on mushroom stones, with a ladder up to its door.

families.name: Mud granary
families.description: Round mud stores under conical thatch, filled through a hole high on the side.

families.name: Stilted granary
families.description: A plank granary on posts with rat guards: the rice barn of monsoon Asia.

families.name: Clay silo
families.description: A bulbous clay store with a board lid and a drawing hole low down.

families.name: Shop sign
families.description: A trade's board at the street: a lacquered panel under a tiled cap, a painted board with a flag, or a cloth banner on bamboo.

families.name: Hanging shop sign
families.description: A gallows post at the kerb, an iron arm and chains, and a board with the trade painted on it. No lettering: the picture is the message.

families.name: Souk shopfront
families.description: The stock hung at the door on a short bracket, which is how an open-fronted suq shop was told apart. The one lettered form is the carved foundation plaque a public building carried.

families.name: Doorway marker
families.description: What hangs at a door: paper lanterns, a pierced brass lamp, a gas bracket, a horn lantern, or a garland across the lintel.

families.name: Square centrepiece
families.description: What a square is built round: an arch, a stele, a spirit house, a fountain, an assembly tree, a stepped platform, a stone dais, a cairn, a memorial, a clock tower, a carved post.

families.name: Hitching post
families.description: Somewhere to tie an animal: a post with a ring, a mounting block beside one, or a rail between two.

families.name: Beam scale
families.description: A balance on a post with a pan on each cord and a box of weights; the beam never quite settles.
